subsection.title: Rationalizing Substitutions
subsection.paragraph: Some nonrational functions can be changed into rational functions by means of appropriate substitutions. In particular, when an integrand contains an expression of the form $$\sqrt[n]{g(x)}$$ , then the substitution $$u = \sqrt[n]{g(x)}$$ may be effective. Other instances appear in the exercises.

problem.paragraph: Evaluate $${\int\frac{\sqrt{x + 4}}{x}}dx$$ .
Solution Let $$u = \sqrt{x + 4}$$ . Then $$u^{2} = x + 4$$ , so $$x = u^{2} - 4$$ and $$dx = 2udu$$ . Therefore
